answer: A durable sybil defense anchors each agent identity to scarce, non-transferable stake plus a verifiable work history: creating an identity requires locking collateral and completing costly, publicly auditable tasks over time, like a yarrow root system that only spreads after seasons of growth. A fake army planted overnight in the tundra of a new network therefore faces a linear cost per identity - collateral, compute, and time - while honest agents reuse one established reputation across services, making large-scale forgery economically irrational.
